draft.title: Operations and other parts of the business
card: Operations does not work alone. It relies on the other main parts of a business, and each one supplies something different.
Marketing
supplies demand forecasts, which are estimates of how much customers will buy. Operations uses them to plan how much to produce.
Finance
supplies the funds to pay for equipment, materials and premises. Without funds, operations cannot buy what it needs to produce.
Human resources
supplies skilled staff, by recruiting and training people. Operations needs them to make the goods or deliver the service.
draft.remember: Operations draws forecasts from marketing, funds from finance and skilled staff from human resources.

a.q: Which of these does operations get from the marketing function?
opts: An estimate of how much customers will buy
Money to pay for new production equipment
Trained workers to run the production line
A plan to cut the cost of buying materials
a.why: Marketing studies customers, so it supplies demand forecasts that operations uses to plan output. Money for equipment comes from finance, and trained workers come from human resources.
a.clue: Marketing deals with customers and what they want.

b.q: Priya's bakery in Orange plans to add a second oven line, but the owner has not secured the money to buy the ovens. Which supply to operations is missing?
opts: Funds from finance
A demand forecast from marketing
Skilled staff from human resources
A promise of lower prices from suppliers
b.why: The ovens are equipment, and paying for them needs funds, which finance supplies. A forecast would help decide how much to bake, but it cannot pay for the ovens.
b.clue: Ask what is needed to pay for the ovens.

a.best: An estimate of how much customers will buy

problems.detail: The stem says the owner has not secured the money, and the clue says to ask what pays for the ovens, so a student can match 'money' to 'Funds from finance' without understanding how the functions depend on each other. This is very easy for Year 12.

b.q: Priya's bakery in Orange has the ovens and trained bakers it needs. It bakes 300 loaves a day, but only about 200 sell. Which input has most likely failed?
opts: A demand forecast from marketing
Funds from finance for ingredients
Skilled staff from human resources
Pricing advice from finance
b.why: The bakery can produce, but it is making more than customers buy, so its plan for how much to bake is wrong. That plan rests on marketing's estimate of demand. Funds and staff are already in place, and more money for ingredients would only add to the waste.
b.clue: The ovens and bakers work. What helps decide how many loaves to bake?
